{"author": null, "closed_at": null, "collaborating_teams": null, "collaborating_users": null, "created_at": null, "credits": [], "credits_detailed": [], "cve_id": null, "cvss": {"score": 7.1, "vector_string": "CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:H"}, "cvss_severities": {"cvss_v3": {"score": 7.1, "vector_string": "CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:H"}, "cvss_v4": {"score": null, "vector_string": null}}, "cwe_ids": ["CWE-400", "CWE-923"], "cwes": [{"cwe_id": "CWE-400", "name": "Uncontrolled Resource Consumption"}, {"cwe_id": "CWE-923", "name": "Improper Restriction of Communication Channel to Intended Endpoints"}], "description": "### Impact

The `allow-webhooks` NetworkPolicy, installed by default with the Flux CLI, admits ingress to notification-controller from every namespace with no port listed. This exposes the event server on port `9090`, whose only security boundary is namespace isolation, to every pod in the cluster.

The result is that any compromised or malicious workload in any namespace, can inject forged Flux events. The practical consequences are:
- denial of service against the event server and the downstream notification providers
- forged alerts in other tenants' notification channels (Slack/Teams/PagerDuty/etc)
- attacker-authored comments posted to tenants' pull requests where the attacker knows the PR URL
- forged commit statuses where the attacker knows a commit hash in the target repository

### Patches

The `allow-webhooks` network policy has been patched in [PR#6028](https://github.com/fluxcd/flux2/pull/6028) and released in Flux [v2.9.4](https://github.com/fluxcd/flux2/releases/tag/v2.9.4).

The DoS mitigation for the event server has been implemented in [PR#1361](https://github.com/fluxcd/notification-controller/pull/1361) and released in notification-controller [v1.9.3](https://github.com/fluxcd/notification-controller/releases/tag/v1.9.2), which is included in the Flux v2.9.4 distribution.

### Workarounds

On clusters that cannot be upgraded immediately, admins can apply the port restriction as a [bootstrap customization](https://fluxcd.io/flux/installation/configuration/bootstrap-customization/):

```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
resources:
  - gotk-components.yaml
  - gotk-sync.yaml
patches:
  - patch: |
      - op: add
        path: /spec/ingress/0/ports
        value:
          - protocol: TCP
            port: 9292
    target:
      kind: NetworkPolicy
      name: allow-webhooks
```

### Credits

This vulnerability was discovered by @stefanprodan during an internal security review of Flux disto, carried out with the assistance of Anthropic LLMs.
